title: Writing for justice: elementary teacher candidates' social justice integration in interdisciplinary units
abstract: Purpose This study investigates how teacher candidates (TCs) in two distinct teacher preparation pathways developed interdisciplinary literacy-rich social studies (SS) units, integrating writing and social justice themes. Design/methodology/approach Using a concurrent mixed-methods design, we analyzed 17 integrated English Language Arts and SS units produced by an elementary Bachelor of Science in Education (BSE) cohort and Master of Arts in Teaching (MAT) cohort for evidence of awareness, inclusive practices, critical practices and transformative practices. Findings The MAT cohort demonstrated more critical and transformative practices across literacy and SS integration, despite receiving no additional scaffolding. The BSE cohort tended to emphasize inclusive practices through text selection. Research limitations/implications Findings are drawn from two cohorts across two programs and may not be generalizable, though they provide insight into preservice teacher development. Practical implications Preparation programs can strengthen equity-focused practice by embedding scaffolds for anti-racist and transformative pedagogy within standards-aligned instruction. Social implications Supporting preservice teachers in socially just practice can advance equity in classrooms, addressing persistent opportunity gaps. Originality/value This study highlights how program type, diversity and prior professional experiences shape TCs' ability to integrate literacy, writing and social justice in standards-aligned SS instruction.

title: When Some are More Equal than Others: Instances of the First-, Second-, and Third-Level Digital Divide Among Slovak Young People from Different Socio-Economic Backgrounds
abstract: Abstract This article uses Digital Inequality Theory as a conceptual lens to explore how young people’s socio-economic background (SES), in interplay with other aspects of their social circumstances, relates to their everyday engagement with digital media in Slovakia. Drawing on a secondary, re-contextualised qualitative analysis of two datasets collected in 2015–2019 and 2022–2024, it examines possible instances of digital inequalities in access, material conditions, digital skills, patterns of use, and tangible outcomes. In the earlier material, inequalities in physical and material access and digital skills were particularly apparent among Roma participants from a socially excluded community. In the later material, differences in basic physical access were less apparent, while material inequalities were evident in device quality and access to paid digital services. Tangible benefits appeared to be associated with broader life circumstances rather than SES alone. The findings challenge assumptions of young people as a homogeneous group of “digital natives” and illustrate how digital inequalities may take diverse and subtle forms. The study highlights the importance of strengthening digital and media literacy education.

title: Two-step approach: Stone extraction after covered stent placement in Mirizzi syndrome: Early experience from a retrospective study
abstract: BACKGROUND Mirizzi syndrome is characterized by large impacted stones and concomitant relative stenosis of the distal bile duct, and its management poses significant clinical challenges. The optimal endoscopic therapeutic strategy for this condition remains a subject of active debate in clinical practice. AIM To investigate endoscopic therapeutic approaches for Mirizzi syndrome. METHODS This was a retrospective, non-controlled, observational study conducted at Renji Hospital, School of Medicine, Shanghai Jiao Tong University. All patients were diagnosed with Mirizzi syndrome and underwent stone extraction after fully covered stent placement between June 2021 and June 2025. Step 1: A fully covered stent was left in the biliary tract for approximately 8 weeks to expand the narrowed bile duct. Step 2: Stent removal and stone extraction using balloons, basket catheters, or electrohydraulic lithotripsy. RESULTS A total of 23 patients (14 females, 9 males; median age 69 years) underwent two-step stent-assisted stone extraction. Fully covered stents were successfully implanted in 23 patients with a median dwell time of 63 days. The stone extraction success rate was 82.6% (19/23) and the median stone extraction time was 21.5 minutes. Five cases of cholecystitis and three cases of pancreatitis were reported. CONCLUSION To our knowledge, this is the first study to evaluate the feasibility and safety of stone extraction after covered stent placement in patients with Mirizzi syndrome. Stone extraction after covered stenting is a viable option for Mirizzi syndrome, particularly in patients unsuitable for prolonged endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography or those with marked distal bile duct stenosis.

title: Transformational leadership and Senge’s learning organization disciplines: developing the integrable but not the integrator
abstract: Purpose Organizations must continuously learn and transform to survive, and transformational leadership (TL) is, in principle, a main driver of such change. Drawing on Bass’s (1985, 1990) TL model and Senge’s (1990) learning organization (LO) framework, this study aims to explore whether TL can develop Senge’s LO disciplines. Design/methodology/approach This inductive qualitative multiple-case study examines five Jordanian organizations exhibiting Senge’s LO disciplines, selected through purposive sampling, drawing mainly on 44 semi-structured interviews. Findings TL positively affects three of Senge’s five disciplines: personal mastery (PM), mental models (MMs) and shared vision (SV). However, it fails to develop the integrative discipline, systems thinking (ST). TL, therefore, cultivates key building blocks but not the integrator and cannot alone develop Senge’s. Practical implications Leaders can use individualized consideration (IC) to develop PM, intellectual stimulation (IS) to challenge MMs and idealized influence (II) to foster SV. They can also explore developing ST through IS. Originality/value This study offers a pathway toward developing LO disciplines through three contributions. First, this paper provides novel empirical evidence for three specific TL component–LO discipline linkages: II–SV, IS–MM and IC–PM. Second, this study identifies TL’s limited capacity to foster ST, while suggesting that IS may conditionally foster it under environmental dynamism, a proposition for future research. Third, its inductive design offers granular, evidence-based analysis of which TL components relate to which LO disciplines, strengthening foundations for future theory-building.

title: Thermal Inactivation Parameters of Salmonella in Lipid-Based Nutrient Supplements
abstract: Abstract Thermal inactivation of Salmonella enterica (8-strain cocktail) was evaluated in three lipid-based nutrient supplement (LNS) formulations with low water activity (0.30 - 0.34): peanut-based (PB), chickpea-based (CP), and a high-fat/high-sugar worst-case (WC) matrix made using the PB product. Inoculated samples were subjected to controlled thermal treatments from 87 to 115 °C, for 5 to 1200 s depending on temperature, and kinetic parameters for Salmonella inactivation were determined. Across products, inactivation followed a log-linear behavior, with R² > 0.90 for most primary-model fits. CP exhibited the highest z-value (22.1 °C), followed by WC (19.2 °C) and PB (17.8 °C). Pairwise analysis confirmed that CP and PB differed significantly in z-value ( p < 0.05), indicating that incremental temperature increases are less effective in the CP formulation. These results show that Salmonella thermal resistance in these three LNS is formulation-dependent, and that processing conditions validated in one LNS cannot be generalized to others. Given the targeted population for LNS distribution, procurement specifications may require manufacturers to demonstrate validated processes capable of achieving ≥5-log reduction of Salmonella to ensure an adequate safety margin. This study provides product-specific kinetic data and underscores the need for independent validation of lethality steps in different LNS formulations.

title: The effects of corrective feedback timing and explicitness on second language learning in video-based computer-mediated communication
journal: International Review of Applied Linguistics in Language Teaching
abstract: Abstract Despite growing attention to the role of corrective feedback (CF) timing in face-to-face or text-based computer-mediated communication (CMC), little is known about how timing and feedback explicitness jointly affect learning in video-based contexts. This study examines the impact of CF timing and explicitness on Chinese EFL learners’ acquisition of the English “be” passive. 68 Participants were randomly assigned to one of five groups (immediate implicit, immediate explicit, delayed implicit, delayed explicit or no-feedback) and performed two communicative tasks conducted via synchronous video conferencing. Learning gains were measured through a pretest-posttest1-posttest2 design using an untimed grammaticality judgement test (UGJT) and an elicited imitation test (EIT). All feedback groups showed significant gains over time on both measures. For the UGJT, a significant interaction between feedback timing and explicitness was found at Posttest 1, although no pairwise contrast remained significant. The delayed implicit feedback group showed delayed gains over time. For the EIT, no significant adjusted group effects or interactions were found. These findings suggest that feedback timing and explicitness should be considered together and are consistent with the view that delayed feedback may promote explicit processing even when implicit in form.

title: The Effectiveness of Classical Guidance Services Using Self-Reflection Techniques to Enhance Self-Disclosure among Grade X Students at SMAN 6 Pandeglang
abstract: Self-disclosure enables adolescents to communicate their thoughts, feelings, and experiences, yet tenth-grade students at SMAN 6 Pandeglang remain hesitant to share their concerns. This study aimed to describe students’ self-disclosure and examine the potential of classroom guidance incorporating self-reflection to improve this ability. A quasi-experimental nonequivalent control group design was employed, involving 72 students selected through purposive sampling and comprising 36 students in each group. Data were collected using a self-disclosure scale and analysed using t-tests. The experimental group’s mean score increased from 95.83 at pretest to 110.08 at posttest, while the control group’s mean increased from 100.61 to 103.92. A paired-samples t-test indicated a statistically significant pretest–posttest increase within the experimental group (p < .001). This observed improvement suggests that classroom guidance incorporating self-reflection may support students’ self-disclosure. The study provides contextual evidence for integrating self-reflection into school guidance and counselling services, with potential implications for supporting adolescents’ self-awareness and interpersonal communication.

title: Structural performance and flexural behaviour of graphene oxide-modified recycled aggregate concrete beams
abstract: Recycled coarse aggregate (RCA) offers a sustainable alternative to natural coarse aggregate. However, its application in structural concrete can be affected by adhered mortar, increased porosity, and the characteristics of the interfacial transition zone. This study experimentally investigates the flexural behaviour of reinforced concrete beams incorporating 100% RCA, manufactured sand (M-sand), and graphene oxide (GO). Six reinforced concrete beams (1,400 × 150 × 150 mm) incorporating GO dosages of 0%, 0.02%, 0.03%, 0.04%, 0.05%, and 0.06% by weight of cement were cast and tested under two-point loading after 28 days of water curing. The first visible cracking load ranged from 14.3 kN for the control beam to 30.5 kN for the beam containing 0.04% GO. The measured peak load of the 0.04% GO beam was 68.6 kN, compared with 40.1 kN for the control beam. Calculated flexural capacities varied from 69.3 kN to 71.8 kN, indicating relatively small differences in theoretical flexural resistance among the mixtures. Energy absorption was evaluated up to first cracking, at a common midspan deflection of 6.5 mm, and up to the maximum recorded load using the measured load–deflection curves. Compared with the control beam, the 0.04% GO beam exhibited higher energy absorption at all three evaluation points, with first-cracking energy increasing from 17.88 J to 57.95 J, energy absorption at 6.5 mm increasing from 156 J to 290 J, and energy absorption up to the maximum recorded load increasing from 206.72 J to 617.76 J. These results indicate that the 0.04% GO beam exhibited the most favourable cracking, peak-load, and energy-absorption responses among the specimens tested. However, because only one beam was tested for each mixture, the findings should be interpreted as experimental observations rather than conclusive evidence of an optimum GO dosage or a general improvement in structural performance.
